newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 26.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 26.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
CANNES - Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon & Eckhardt, the U.S.
advertising group, is expected to announce soon a link with a
network of similar size. Advertising and banking sources told
Reuters possible partners were Havas Advertising and True North,
which owns Foote Cone & Belding and just finalised its "divorce"
from France's Publicis.
CANNES - Booming economies and expanding TV markets in Asia
are fuelling double-digit growth in advertising, with key
markets such as China offering vast growth opportunities,
according to advertising executives. Asia's growing clout in the
world of marketing was driven home by the arrival at the
festival in Cannes of a 350-strong delegation from China.
CANNES - A wordless advertisement for Mercedes Benz created
by the London office of Leo Burnett wins the top award in the
Press & Poster category at the 1997 International Advertising
Festival.
FRANKFURT - Rising costs coupled with lower advertising
budgets mean German firms are demanding more effective
advertising, according to an industry survey from the GWA
advertisers federation.
WASHINGTON - The U.S. Supreme Court upholds a federal
programme that requires California fruit growers to chip in for
industrywide, generic advertising campaigns, saying it is not a
violation of free speech rights.
FRANKFURT - More German companies are using phone numbers in
ads advertising to attract customers, German direct marketing
federation DDV says.
NEW YORK - Continental Airlines suspends its advertising
campaign in New York City urging the city's travellers to fly
from New Jersey's Newark International Airport instead of JFK,
following complaints by New York's mayor.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
LONDON - Scantily-clad "babes" are boosting sales of British
men's magazines, according to a report published by Euromonitor,
a market research company. Sales of men's lifestyle magazines
will reach 80 million pounds ($133.4 million) this year, almost
double last year's figure.
BRUSSELS - The Belgian VTM commercial TV channel says it
will claim 15 to 20 billion francs ($420-560 million) in damages
from the Flemish regional government if it loses its advertising
monopoly. The European Commission is expected to tell Belgium it
must scrap VTM's monopoly or face legal action.
LONDON - Britain's Independent Television Commission
watchdog says it's confident in its decision to award three key
licences to run digital terrestrial television, despite a
possible legal challenge. Digital Television Network says it
might seek legal redress and challenge the ITC's decision to
award the licences to its rival British Digital Broadcasting
consortium.
NEW YORK - Cahners Publishing Co, the U.S. publishing unit
of Reed Elsevier, expects to post a 15 percent gain in operating
income in 1998.
MAKUHARI, Japan - PointCast Inc, the U.S.-based
Internet-related company, says it will launch a
Japanese-language version in September of its personalised news
service that using "push" technology.
MEXICO CITY - Mexico's private television network TV Azteca
estimates that it will capture about a third of the country's
total $1.2 billion TV advertising market this year.
PARIS - ABSat signs accord with Compagnie Generale des Eaux
under which nine of its 20 channels would be broadcast on the
digital service offered by CGE's cable television unit
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
BEIJING - The Chinese side of a troubled joint venture with
Peugeot SA has vowed to continue car production alone or with
new partners if the French company pulls out, the Economic Daily
says.
PRAGUE - Czechbrewe Budejovicky Budvar says it will soon
brew and export a powerful version of its lager to be called
"Bud", firing another shot in the tiny brewery's battle with
Anheuser Busch in the United States.
LONDON - Three years after their union, Rover and BMW are
about to deliver their first new product -- the baby Land Rover
called the Freelander.
HONG KONG - Looming Chinese rule over Hong Kong will not
scare away tourists and the territory will remain a mecca for
travellers, a senior tourism official says.
LONDON - Britain's biggest retail pharmacist, Boots Co Plc,
will open its first store in Thailand as part of plans to expand
its Boots the Chemist chain internationally.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
LONDON - Most Europeans do not trust their governments to
protect them from the possible dangers of genetically-modified
food, researchers from the London School of Economics say.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong officials say China's 1.2-
billion-strong population represents a voracious market not just
for consumer goods like automobiles and televisions but for
narcotics like heroin.
TOKYO - Consumers are so keen on Tamagotchi virtual pet toys
that the company that makes them, Bandai Co Ltd, is considering
raising production to 10 million units a month once it starts
full-scale sales of the toys in overseas markets. It now
produces two to three million a month.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong women are paying $1,000 a time for
beauty makeovers before going to parties celebrating Hong Kong's
return to China, report local beauty salons.
